info.title: Syncro
info.description:
Welcome to the official Syncro API Docs.

To use these docs, you will need an active Syncro account. You can sign up for one here: [Syncro](https://syncromsp.com)

If you already have an active account, fill in your subdomain below and then click "Authorize" and fill in your api-key. The key is specific to your user account so it is found on the your user profile page.

Please review the [API License Agreement](https://syncromsp.com/syncromsp-api-license-agreement/) before using our API. By accessing our API, you are agreeing to the API License Agreement.

Please note there is a rate limit of 180 requests per minute per IP address on API Usage.

get.summary: Returns a paginated list of Contracts
get.description:
Required permission: Contracts - List/Search

Every contract in the list carries the same covered-item fields as `GET /contracts/{id}`.

Covered items are part of the contract payload:

* `product_price_overrides` — the covered products with their contracted rate
  (`price_retail_cents` or `discount_percentage`) and their block-list status
  (`blacklisted`, meaning the product is billed separately from the contract).
* `non_billable_product_ids` — products covered by the contract and therefore not
  billed on their own.
* `schedule_ids` — the recurring invoice schedules this contract governs. Link a
  schedule to a contract by sending `contract_id` to the Schedule endpoints.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Returns provided page of results, each 'page' contains 50 results

post.description:
Required permission: Contracts - Edit

A complete contract — top-level attributes, covered items with their contracted
rates, the block-list and the non-billable products — is created in this one call.

Covered items are part of the contract payload:

* `product_price_overrides` — the covered products with their contracted rate
  (`price_retail_cents` or `discount_percentage`) and their block-list status
  (`blacklisted`, meaning the product is billed separately from the contract).
* `non_billable_product_ids` — products covered by the contract and therefore not
  billed on their own.
* `schedule_ids` — the recurring invoice schedules this contract governs. Link a
  schedule to a contract by sending `contract_id` to the Schedule endpoints.

product_price_overrides.description: The products the contract covers, with their contracted rates and block-list status. Replaces the whole set: omit the key to leave the existing overrides untouched, or send an empty array to remove them all. An entry with an `id` updates that existing override, an entry without one creates a new override, and any existing override whose `id` is not listed is deleted. Set either `price_retail_cents` or `discount_percentage` (never both) unless `blacklisted` is true. Must be a JSON array of objects — anything else, including an array containing `null`, is rejected with 422 rather than treated as an empty set. Clearing the set requires a JSON body, since a form-encoded empty array cannot be transmitted.

id.description: Existing override to update; omit to create a new one

price_retail_cents.description: Contracted rate for the product, in cents

discount_percentage.description: Percentage off the catalog price, greater than 0 and at most 100

blacklisted.description: Block-list the product so it is billed separately from the contract

non_billable_product_ids.description: Products covered by the contract and therefore not billed separately. Replaces the whole set; omit the key to leave it untouched. Must be a JSON array of integers — anything else, including an array containing `null`, is rejected with 422 rather than treated as an empty set. Clearing the set requires a JSON body, since a form-encoded empty array cannot be transmitted.

requestBody.description: Contract object that needs to be added

post.description:
Required permission: Invoices - Create

`subtotal`, `total`, `tax`, `balance_due`, `is_paid`, `verified_paid`, `tech_marked_paid`,
`pdf_url`, `customer_business_then_name` and `hardwarecost` are computed from the line
items and payments. They are returned on every response but ignored in a request; this
endpoint has never accepted them.

number.description: Defaults to your account's next invoice number.

employee.description: Read-only on create: always set to the email address of the API token's owner, so a value sent here is discarded. Settable with `PUT /invoices/{id}`.

paid.description: Take payment for the invoice as soon as it is created. Only applies when `line_items` are sent in the same call.

product_id.description: When given, `item`, `name`, `cost`, `price` and `taxable` default from the product.

item.description: Also used to look the product up by name when no `product_id` or `upc_code` is given.

product_id.description: When a product is resolved — by `product_id`, `upc_code` or `item` — it **overrides** `cost`, `price` and `taxable`, whatever you send. `item` and `name` are only defaulted from it when you send neither. (`POST /invoices` differs: there a product only fills in the fields you omit.)

upc_code.description: Look the product up by barcode instead of by id.

price.description: Ignored when a product is resolved — the product's price wins.

cost.description: Ignored when a product is resolved — the product's cost wins.

taxable.description: When a product is resolved the line is taxable only if both this and the product are, so `false` here always wins and `true` defers to the product.

location_id.description: Required on multi-location accounts when the invoice has no location.

Required permission: Purchase Orders - Edit

Accepts a single file via `multipart/form-data`. The file's actual content
(detected via magic-byte sniffing) must be one of the allowed types
(JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, CSV, XLS, XLSX) and the filename extension must match
the detected type. The declared `Content-Type` header is informational only

post.description:
Required permission: Recurring Invoices - New

Accepts every settable field on a schedule, so a schedule can be fully configured in one
call. Add its line items afterwards with `POST /schedules/{id}/line_items`, or seed them
from an existing invoice by passing `invoice_id`.

`id`, `account_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `last_run` are read-only. So are
`subscription_status` and `recurring_type_id`, which are maintained for you: the first is
recomputed from the linked contract and the unpaid invoice count on every run, and the second
is what selects the billing engine for the whole schedule.

Every id in the request is checked against your account before anything is written, so a
rejected request changes nothing. Errors come back as
`{"error": ["Location can't be found", ...]}` with status 422.

200.description: Fully configured in a single call

error: Frequency Must be a valid selection

next_run.description: Date of the next run, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Any other format is rejected with 422 `{"error": "Sorry, unable to read the date, use this format: Y-m-d"}`.

contract_id.description: Contract this schedule is billed under. Must belong to the same customer as the schedule.

location_id.description: Location the generated invoices belong to.

user_id.description: Employee credited with the generated invoices, for commission.

invoice_term_id.description: Billing terms applied to the generated invoices.

template_id.description: Invoice template used to render the generated invoices. Must be an invoice template. Defaults to the account's.

source_id.description: The schedule this one was copied from. Recorded for reference only — it does not copy anything. Use `invoice_id` on create to seed line items.

invoice_id.description: Create only, and not stored on the schedule: the schedule's line items are seeded from this invoice's line items. Must be an invoice on your account.

period_mode_id.description: Which billing period the generated invoice covers. `0` in arrears (period ends on the invoice date), `3` in arrears exclusive (ends the day before), `1` in advance (starts the day after), `2` in advance inclusive (starts on the invoice date).

last_day_of_month.description: Move each run to the last day of its month.

paused.description: A paused schedule generates nothing until it is resumed.

generated_invoice_name.description: Name given to each invoice this schedule generates.

memo.description: Memo copied onto the generated invoices.

keep_pricing_current.description: Re-price every line from the current product price on each run, instead of holding the price captured when the line was added.

allow_blank_invoices.description: Generate an invoice even when the run produces no lines.

email_customer.description: Email the generated invoice to the customer.

snail_mail.description: Post the generated invoice to the customer.

email_receipt.description: Email the customer a receipt after a successful charge.

charge_mop.description: Auto-charge the stored payment method. Without a `payment_id` the schedule still generates invoices but charges nothing and records a failed payment on each run.

payment_id.description: Stored payment method to auto-charge. Must be a payment profile belonging to this schedule's customer.

charge_on_due_date.description: Charge on the invoice due date rather than on the run date. Only meaningful together with `invoice_term_id`.

apply_credit.description: Spend any available customer credit against the generated invoice.

reset_prepay_hours.description: Reset the customer's prepaid hours on each run.

invoice_unbilled_ticket_charges.description: Pull the customer's unbilled ticket charges onto the generated invoice.

invoice_unbilled_ticket_statuses.description: Restrict the unbilled ticket charges to tickets in these statuses. Send either a comma-separated string or a JSON array of strings; both are stored comma-separated. Every status must exist on your account. Blank means all statuses.

unbilled_ticket_charge_order.description: Order the unbilled ticket charges are added in.

create_ticket_on_failed_billing.description: Open a ticket when a run fails to bill.

create_ticket_one_month_prior_to_end.description: Open a ticket a month before the linked contract ends.

schedule_retry_card_on_failed_billing.description: Retry the stored card later when a charge fails.

post.summary: Adds a Line Item to an Invoice Schedule
post.description:
Required permission: Recurring Invoices - Edit

A new line needs either a `name` or a `product_id` to take one from. Most other fields only
apply to one kind of line, chosen with `recurring_type_id`; the descriptions say which.
`POST /schedules/{id}/add_line_item` is an older alias for this endpoint and behaves
identically.

product_id.description: Product billed by this line. When given, `name`, `description` and `product_category` default from the product.

name.description: Label shown on the generated invoice line. Defaults from the product's name when `product_id` is given.

description.description: Longer text shown under the name. Defaults from the product's description when `product_id` is given.

quantity.description: Ignored for the line types that derive their own quantity (asset, contact, remote access, policy folder, vendor and Kabuto subscriptions).

price_retail.description: Price charged, in currency units. Alternative to `retail_cents`.

price_cost.description: Your cost, in currency units. Alternative to `cost_cents`.

position.description: Sort order on the generated invoice. Defaults to the bottom of the list.

product_category.description: Overwritten by the product's own category when `product_id` is given.

one_time_charge.description: Bill this line once and then stop, rather than on every run.

user_id.description: Employee credited with the line. Defaults to the owner of the API token.

recurring_type_id.description: What kind of line this is, which decides how its quantity is calculated. `1` recurring invoice, `2` data backup, `3` general subscription, `4` asset, `5` Kabuto, `6` contact, `7` Syncro Backup, `8` remote access, `9` policy folder, `10` third-party vendor, `11` Cloudberry.

asset_type_id.description: Asset subscriptions (`recurring_type_id` 4): bill for the customer's assets of this type.

saved_asset_search_id.description: Asset subscriptions: bill for the assets matching this saved search instead of an asset type.

contact_field_type_id.description: Contact subscriptions (`recurring_type_id` 6): bill for contacts by this custom field.

contact_field_answer_id.description: Contact subscriptions: bill only for contacts whose answer to that field is this one.

policy_folder_id.description: Policy folder subscriptions (`recurring_type_id` 9): bill for the assets in this folder.

bill_nested_folders.description: Policy folder subscriptions: include assets in the folder's sub-folders.

vendor_name.description: Third-party vendor lines (`recurring_type_id` 10): the vendor to read usage from.

vendor_product_name.description: Third-party vendor lines: the vendor product to bill.

bill_all_units.description: Bill every unit reported, rather than only those over `bill_units_threshold`.

bill_units_threshold.description: Number of units included before billing starts. Required when `bill_all_units` is false.

include_zero_charge.description: Keep the line on the invoice even when it bills nothing.

m365_unit_type.description: Microsoft 365 vendor lines: bill licensed (`all`) or consumed (`consumed`) seats.

syncro_backup_billing_type.description: Syncro Backup lines (`recurring_type_id` 7): bill per licence or per GB of cloud storage.

syncro_backup_credit_type.description: Syncro Backup storage lines: whether the included storage is a global or per-asset allowance.

syncro_backup_bill_all.description: Syncro Backup lines: bill all usage, ignoring the included allowance.

syncro_backup_bill_after_licenses.description: Syncro Backup licence lines: licences included before billing starts.

syncro_backup_bill_after_storage.description: Syncro Backup storage lines: GB included before billing starts.

post.summary: Creates a Ticket Timer that starts running
post.description:
Required permission: Ticket Timers - Overview

Creates a Ticket Timer that starts directly in status_running (start_time is set to
now, end_time is left unset). The timer always belongs to the authenticated
technician — any client-supplied user_id is ignored.

A technician holds at most one active timer per ticket. If they already have a running or
paused timer on the ticket it is resumed and returned with a 200 rather than a second timer
being created, and the request body is ignored.

An omitted or null `billable` resolves to the account's "time is non-billable by default"
setting, matching the Web App.

200.description: the technician already has an active timer on the ticket

patch.summary: Updates an existing Ticket Timer by ID

errors: Billable must be true or false

requestBody.description: Ticket Timer object that needs to be updated

post.summary: Starts (or resumes a paused) Ticket Timer
post.description:
Required permission: Ticket Timers - Overview

Starts a Ticket Timer that has never been started, or resumes a paused one. Returns a
422 if the timer is already running or has been stopped.

errors: Ticket timer cannot transition from status 'status_running'

post.description:
Required permission: Ticket Timers - Overview

Pauses a running Ticket Timer. Returns a 422 if the timer is not currently running.

errors: Ticket timer cannot transition from status 'status_paused'

post.summary: Stops a running or paused Ticket Timer
post.description:
Required permission: Ticket Timers - Overview

Stops a running or paused Ticket Timer. Returns a 422 if the timer is already stopped.
If the account has `ticket_timer_charge_by_default` enabled, this also creates the

get.summary: Returns a paginated flat list of comments across multiple tickets
get.description:
Required permissions: "Tickets - View Details" or "Tickets - View 'Their Ticket' Details (assigned to them)"

Returns a flat, paginated list of comments across multiple tickets sorted by
ticket_id ASC, created_at DESC. All comments for a given ticket are adjacent
in the response, with the newest comments first within each ticket.

Comments can be scoped to specific tickets using a saved Ticket View
(ticket_search_id) and/or direct ticket filters such as customer_id, status, etc.

Comment-level date filters use the `comment_` prefix to distinguish them from
the ticket-level date filters that share similar names (e.g. created_after).

Single-Customer Users can only access comments for their own tickets.

parameters.name: ticket_search_id
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets matching this saved Ticket View (Ticket Search) ID

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: Scope results to a specific ticket

parameters.description: Scope results to tickets belonging to this customer

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets belonging to this contact

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets assigned to this user

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets with this status. Use 'Not Closed' to exclude resolved tickets.

parameters.name: resolved_after
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets resolved after this date

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets created after this date

parameters.name: since_updated_at
parameters.description: Scope results to tickets updated after this date

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: When true, scope results to tickets assigned to the authenticated user

parameters.name: comment_created_after
parameters.description: Filter comments created after this date

parameters.name: comment_created_before
parameters.description: Filter comments created before this date

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of results to return. Default is 1.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of comments per page. Default is 25, maximum is 100.

parameters.name: comment_format
parameters.description: Body format for comments. Allowed values: 'plaintext' (default), 'richtext', 'original'.
